scenarios.nfr_ref: PRD AC-045 dashboard latency (S2 leg: write-path)
scenarios.description: Single-row apply_inward call latency against testcontainers PG. Sets a sanity threshold for S2 write-path so S3's read-path latency budget isn't already consumed by writes.
7-day backdate window boundary: purchase_date = today-7 accepted; purchase_date = today-8 rejected with ERR-002.
Malformed POST /api/v1/inward payloads rejected at the API boundary with 422; sending a non-int nos string is intercepted by Pydantic before service code runs.
scenarios.expected: All three return HTTP 422 with descriptive detail; no rows inserted

scenarios.description: TC-087 functional verification: two concurrent threads, each holding their own SQLAlchemy session against the SAME testcontainer engine, both invoke apply_inward for the SAME (design, grade) starting from balance > 0. SELECT FOR UPDATE must serialize them. Final ledger has 2 new rows with running_balance increasing monotonically.

execution_results.details: 50 samples + 3 warmups against testcontainers PG. Way under budget — S3 will have ample latency budget for read-path.
parametrized [days_ago=7, accepted] and [days_ago=8, rejected with ValidationError] both verified. AC-021 boundary precisely enforced.
parametrized [nos='abc', missing_field=supplier_id, nos=-1] all returned HTTP 422 with descriptive detail; no InwardHeader rows persisted. Pydantic + DB CHECK defense-in-depth verified.

execution_results.iteration_1_outcome: FAIL — race condition discovered: both threads got running_balance=15 instead of [15, 20]. Root cause: PostgreSQL SELECT ... LIMIT 1 ORDER BY ... FOR UPDATE doesn't re-resolve LIMIT after waiting on a row lock; the second waiter re-reads the originally-identified row (now-stale prior latest) instead of the row just inserted by the first writer. Documented as TD-011.
execution_results.iteration_1_fix: Added pg_advisory_xact_lock(design_id, grade_id) BEFORE the FOR UPDATE in domain.stock._apply. Advisory lock serializes all writes per (design, grade) and auto-releases at txn commit.
execution_results.iteration_2_outcome: PASS — final balances [10, 15, 20] confirmed; lock now correctly serializes.
execution_results.iteration_2_secondary_issue: ST-007's raw-SessionLocal commits (outside db_session rollback fixture) polluted the shared testcontainer PG with leftover rows, breaking 3 downstream seed tests. Added try/finally cleanup deleting design + grade + map + ledger rows. Full backend suite: 112/112 PASS.
execution_results.details: Two concurrent threads on separate sessions, both calling apply_inward(nos=5) starting from balance=10 → final running_balance must be 20 (not 15). After fix: confirmed correct serialization. HLD R-001 mitigation verified end-to-end with real 2-session concurrency.

discoveries: DS-002 implementation gap: SELECT ... LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE alone is insufficient for serializing writes against the 'lock the latest row' pattern. Advisory lock added to close the gap. TD-011 logged.

new_tech_debt.description: DS-002 documented 'SELECT FOR UPDATE on latest row' as the serialization primitive, but PostgreSQL's SELECT ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE has a documented gotcha: when the originally-identified row is locked by another txn, the waiter re-reads that ORIGINAL row after the lock releases — NOT the new latest row inserted by the holder. ST-007 surfaced this with a real 2-session test. Fixed in T-045 (_apply) by acquiring pg_advisory_xact_lock(design_id, grade_id) BEFORE the FOR UPDATE row lock. DS-002's intent (serialize writes per (design, grade)) is now satisfied; the FOR UPDATE row lock remains as defense-in-depth.
